title: Antibiotic Sensitivity Test for Dinoflagellates and Chromera
author: Yoshihisa Hirakawa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vcke2uw

steps.title: Grow cultures in flasks
steps.instruction: Inoculate each of the seven dinoflagellate species (Amphidinium carterae, Glenodinium foliaceum, Heterocapsa triquetra, Karlodinium veneficum, Prorocentrum minimum, Symbiodinium minutum, Togula britannica) and Chromera velia into 75 mL plastic flasks containing Daikin IMK (Nihon Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.) medium, f/2 medium, or ESM medium. Incubate at 20 °C under white illumination of 60 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ on a 14 h light : 10 h dark cycle.

steps.title: Transfer cells and add antibiotics
steps.instruction: Transfer the precultured cells to 24‑well plates so that the starting cell density is 2,000–40,000 cells mL⁻¹. Add the chosen antibiotic (puromycin or zeocin) to each well at final concentrations of 0, 50, 100, or 300 µg mL⁻¹. Incubate the plates under the same conditions as above (20 °C, 60 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹, 14:10 light:dark).

steps.title: Count living cells
steps.instruction: During the following week, count the number of living cells in each well using a microscope and a hemacytometer.
